review_note: All four conditions hold for the 6 rows (spatial_mesh_intercept and spatial_mesh_slope, three links each). (1) The SPDE c0, g1 and g2 are hand-built by finite elements from the triangulation. Q = kappa^4 c0 + 2 kappa^2 g1 + g2. The barycentric projection is also hand-built. These are matched to the package objects (mesh$spde c0/g1/g2 at 1e-9, mesh$A_st at 1e-8), and those expectations are inside the 87 that passed. The likelihood is a base-R dense Laplace with the hand Sigma = solve(Q) and hand projection. The triangulation itself comes from the package mesh (fmesher), which is reasonable. (2) Bugs are asserted at more than 0.1: reversed site SD, precision x 2, kappa doubled, projection nodes reversed, and (for the slope) dropped slope design. Minimum gaps are 1.2 to 2.5, against agreement of 1e-12 to 1e-7. (3) The fits are spatial(1 | site, mesh) with sd(site, level='spatial') ~ z_site, and spatial(0 + x | site, mesh) with coef = 'x'. Kappa is fixed through make_mesh(kappa = 1/1000), and the oracle uses mesh$kappa, so the agreement is at the fixed-kappa precision. This matches mesh_precision_fixed_kappa. (4) The manifest and fragment hashes match. The console log shows 87 expectations, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 errors, and my rerun on Totoro gave 87/0/0/0. This does NOT establish: kappa estimation or kappa-dependent behaviour (kappa is fixed); calibration or recovery; a spatial q2 correlated block; any Julia parity; meshes other than this 32-site regular layout.
